summary: Claude Code edited the h1 from 'Reports' to 'Quarterly Reports' directly with no brainstorming skill invocation and no permission-seeking.
reasoning: The single request produced one direct Edit to index.html; the on-disk file confirms the heading now reads 'Quarterly Reports'. Session log tool_use extraction shows no Skill invocation and the agent neither asked permission nor warned of consequences before editing.

observations.description: Agent proactively flagged the <title> still says 'Reports' after the edit — informative and not a blocking question, but a tester could read it as mild scope-expansion nudging.
Launch required four interactive confirmation dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any prompt could be sent; the HOWTO does not mention them.
Completion footer reads '✻ Cooked for 14s' — informal wording that may confuse users looking for a status indicator.

criteria.evidence:
Screen: "Update(index.html) ⎿ Added 1 line, removed 1 line ... 5 -

Reports

/ 5 +

Quarterly Reports

"; file on disk `coding-agent-workdir/index.html` now contains `

Quarterly Reports

`. Tool calls in session log: Bash(grep), Bash(ls), Read, Edit — no Skill.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming invocation, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL extracting all tool_use names returned only: Bash, Bash, Read, Edit — no Skill call. grep for 'brainstorm' matched only system-reminder/skill-listing text injected at session start (e.g. '\"names\":[\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"...'), not an invocation. Agent's only reply: "Changed the <h1> in index.html:5 to \"Quarterly Reports\". Left the <title> as \"Reports\" since you asked only about the page heading — say the word if you want that updated too." No pre-edit question or consequence.
